full_judgment:
2. The Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 21013 of 2013 was issued under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the proceedings of CR Case No. 82 of 2012 under section 420 of the Penal Code now pending in the court of Judicial Magistrate, Pabna, should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. In this case allegation of dishonour of a cheque dated 14-11-2011 amounting to Taka 95,00,000 by the bank for "insufficient fund" was brought. 

 3. The Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 21014 of 2013 was issued under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the proceedings in CR Case No. 111 of 2012 under section 420 of the Penal Code now pending in the court of Judicial Magistrate, Pabna, should not be quashed. In this case allegation of dishonor of a cheque dated 24-8-2011 amounting to Taka 25,00,000 by the bank for "insufficient fund" was brought against the petitioner. 

 4. The Rule in Miscellaneous Case No. 21015 of 2012 was issued under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the proceedings in CR Case No. 70 of 2012, now pending in the court of Judicial Magistrate, Pabna, should not be quashed. In this case allegation of dishonor of a chaque dated 23-1-2011 for Taka 1,30,00,000 by the Bank for "insufficient fund" along with allegation of cheating was brought against the accused- petitioner. 

 5. Relevant facts for disposal of the above mentioned three Rules containing similar facts are, in short, that witness No. 2 Md Abdul Awal Khan entrusted with the accused petitioner an amount of Taka 2,50,00,000 by installments on different dates. For the purpose of making payment of the said amounts, the accused petitioner issued 3(three) cheques dated 23-1¬2011, 24-8-2011 and 14-11-2011 respectively in the name of the witness No. 2, Md Abdul Awal Khan who placed the aforesaid three cheques for encashment on 15-3-2011, 25-9-2011 and 16-11¬2011 respectively to the respective banks but all those cheques were dishonored for "insufficient fund" in the account of the accused petitioner. Knowing the aforesaid fact the accused petitioner assured the witness No. 2 that he would make payment and requested him to wait for sometimes. Giving the aforesaid assurance' the accused petitioner most cunningly passed the prescribed period of initiating legal proceedings. Finally, when the witness No. 2 demanded payment of money in presence of other witnesses on 15-5- 2012, 9-6-2012 and 22-7-2012 respectively, the accused petitioner denied his claim and refused to make payment of the cheque amount to him. Thereafter, the complainant as an authorized person and constituted attorney has filed the instant cases under sections 420/406 of the Penal Code for cheating and misappropriation of the money. 

 6. The accused-petitioner surrendered before the trial court and obtained bail in all the three cases. Later, the trial court fixed the cases for hearing charge and for hearing the application filed by the accused petitioner under section 241A of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking discharge from the cases. The trial court upon hearing rejected the application under section 241A and framed charge under section 420 of the Penal Code against the accused-petitioner. At this juncture, the accused petitioner moved this court by filing the applications under section 561 A of the Code seeking quashment of the impugned proceedings and obtained the present Rules and orders of stay. 

 7. Mr Tajul Islam Miajee, learned Advocate appearing for the accused petitioner submits that the transactions were alleged to have been made in between the witness No. 2 and the accused petitioner but the witness No. 2, Md Abdul Awal Khan did not file any complaint against the petitioner rather the complaints have been filed by a person who had no nexus with the transactions; hence, he has no locus standi to file the instant cases. Moreover, he submits that the cases are preposterous and the allegations so made in the complaint itself constitute no offence against the accused petitioner. 

 8. He also submits that bouncing of cheque simpliciter does not constitute any offence as defined in section 415 of the Penal Code punishable under section 420 and, as such, framing of charge against the accused petitioner under section 420 of the Penal Code is improper and unjust and, as such, the continuation of the proceedings against the petitioner is absolutely an abuse of the process of the court and hence liable to be quashed to secure ends of Justice. In support of his submissions he has referred to the cases of Surendranath Saha vs The State, reported in 12 DLR 178 and MA Sukkur vs Md Zahirul Hoque & another, reported in 5 ALR (AD) 27. 

 11. In the present cases, the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner has raised two pertinent points of law. Firstly, the complaint in three cases have been filed by one Md Shahidul Islam who claims to be an attorney of witness No. 2, Md Abdul Awal Khan is not a person cheated by the accused petitioner and, as such, the complainant has no locus standi to file the complaints against the accused-petitioner. Secondly, the allegations of bouncing of cheque does not constitute any offence as defined in section 415 of the Penal Code and, as such, framing of charge against the accused petitioner under section 420 of the Penal Code suffers from serious illegality. 

 12. On perusal of the complaints it appears that the complaints have been filed by one Md Shahidul Islam describing himself as an attorney of Md Abdul Awal Khan. It also appears that the allegations against the accused petitioner as made in the complaints are that the accused-petitioner cheated Md Abdul Awal Khan who entrusted the money with the accused petitioner. Said Md Abdul Awal Khan has been shown in the complaints as witness No. 2, instead of filing the case by him as complainant. In the case of Surendranath Saha vs State reported in 12 DLR 178 it has been held that; 

 "Where a complaint of cheating before the court has been made not by the person defrauded but by another on his behalf the case must fail." 

 13. In the given context since the complaints in the present cases have not been filed by the person alleged to have been cheated it must be found that the complainant has no locus standi to make a complaint. 

 14. We have gone through another decision referred by the petitioner's counsel reported in MA Sukkur vs Md Zahirul Hoque, 5 ALR (AD) 27. In the said case the accused was a loanee and he made part payment of the loan money to the bank and some of the cheques given were dishonored. But in the present case the accused is a trustee and no part payment was made. As such, the case cited by the petitioner's council is factually distinct and different from the present case in hand. Therefore, it is not applicable in the instant case. 

 The proceedings in CR Case Nos. 70 of 2012, 82 of 2012 and 111 of 2012 now pending before the court of Judicial Magistrate, Pabna, are hereby quashed.
